name: Teapot Dome bribery and contempt cases (1922–1931)
summary: Federal oil-lease scandal. Interior Secretary Albert B. Fall's bribery conviction was affirmed by the D.C. Circuit (Fall v. United States, 49 F.2d 506, 1931); oilman Harry Sinclair's contempt case reached the Supreme Court (Sinclair v. United States, 279 U.S. 263, 1929). Reportedly the oilman accused of paying Fall was acquitted — to be verified.

courts: Supreme Court of the United States
U.S. Court of Appeals, D.C. Circuit

knownPrimarySources.title: Fall v. United States, 49 F.2d 506 (D.C. Cir. 1931)

rationale: The cleanest primary record of the three, including Supreme Court opinions. It offers a striking documented contrast between outcomes for different defendants, a natural reveal structure, and every principal is long deceased.
risks: Corruption rather than violent crime — less instant 'true crime' pull; the hook must come from the documented contrast
Many overlapping proceedings (civil lease cases, Senate contempt, jury-shadowing contempt, bribery trials) — scope must be narrowed
Several trial-level outcomes may not be on CourtListener; newspapers/National Archives needed
notes: Discovery summary from general knowledge — UNVERIFIED. Not a claim; research must verify every element against primary records.
